Install guide

Up and running in a minute.

Doceo isn’t code-signed yet, so your system shows a one-time warning. It’s expected — here’s the quick way past it.

macOS

  1. Open the .dmgDouble-click the file you downloaded.
  2. Drag Doceo to ApplicationsDrop the icon onto the Applications folder in the window.
  3. Right-click Doceo → OpenChoose Open in the dialog. Just double-clicking an unsigned app won’t offer that button — right-click once, and it opens normally from then on.

Linux

  1. AppImage (any distribution)Make it executable, then run it: chmod +x Doceo_0.6.0_amd64.AppImage && ./Doceo_0.6.0_amd64.AppImage. No install needed.
  2. Debian, Ubuntu, Mintsudo apt install ./Doceo_0.6.0_amd64.deb
  3. Fedora, openSUSE, RHELsudo dnf install ./Doceo-0.6.0-1.x86_64.rpm
  4. Needs WebKitGTKDoceo uses your system web view. On most desktops it’s already there; otherwise install webkit2gtk-4.1 from your package manager.

Windows

  1. Run the setup fileDouble-click Doceo_0.6.0_x64-setup.exe.
  2. Click “More info” → “Run anyway”If you see a blue “Windows protected your PC” box, that’s SmartScreen reacting to an unsigned app.
  3. Follow the installerNext → Install. If it offers the WebView2 Runtime, allow it — it’s a small Microsoft component the app needs.
  4. Launch DoceoFrom the Start menu or desktop shortcut.
